title: AstroMemBench: A Benchmark for Memory Systems in Embodied Spacecraft Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.16590v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-term spacecraft autonomy requires embodied agents to use operational history under communication delays, time-critical operations, environmental uncertainty, complex physical interactions, power and computational constraints, and safety and reliability requirements. We introduce AstroMemBench and a Scenario-Challenge-Capability design method that maps these requirements to executable memory tests. The benchmark covers 16 memory subchallenges through 140 templates and 2240 instances across nine tasks in planetary surface operations, on-orbit servicing, and deep-space exploration. A deterministic environment scores actions for task completion, state changes, safety, and resource use. Ablations under nine conditions show that the benchmark is sensitive to how accurately agents recover and use historical information and to differences in memory-system design. translated_title: AstroMemBench：一个面向具身航天器智能体的记忆系统基准测试
tldr: 本文提出 AstroMemBench——一个面向具身航天器智能体的记忆系统基准测试，通过“场景-挑战-能力”设计方法在行星表面作业、在轨服务和深空探测九项任务中构建 16 个记忆子挑战共 2240 个实例，以确定性可复现的方式评估记忆系统设计对智能体利用历史信息能力的影响。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AstroMemBench, a benchmark for memory systems in embodied spacecraft agents, which uses a Scenario-Challenge-Capability design method to generate 16 memory subchallenges across nine tasks in planetary surface operations, on-orbit servicing, and deep-space exploration, with deterministic scoring revealing how memory-system design affects agents' ability to recover and use historical information.
